title: Repeated halving at every splice at 1
question: what changes if every time there is a splice at 1, everything else halves?

verdict.conclusion: halving the horizontal displacement of every zero within the same xi zero set is RH-equivalent, but has not been derived. At finite stages, halving only inherited states cannot exclude new zeros escaping at growing heights. Literal admitted-weight halving destroys the xi limit, while halving the remaining deficit preserves and accelerates that limit without itself controlling zeros.

sameXiZeroContraction.identityTheoremArgument: an off-line xi zero would generate infinitely many distinct xi zeros at the same ordinate, accumulating at the finite point 1/2+i gamma; since xi is entire and nonzero, this is impossible
sameXiZeroContraction.converse: if RH holds, every zero is fixed by H
sameXiZeroContraction.status: the zero-set invariance H(Z(xi)) subset Z(xi) is equivalent to RH, not an independent proof

finiteStageZeroContraction.conditionalTheorem: if every zero of every finite completion obeys |Re(s)-1/2| <= C 2^(-N) and the completions converge locally uniformly to xi, Rouche-Hurwitz transfer forces every xi zero onto the line
finiteStageZeroContraction.trackedOnlyLimitation: the observed finite counts 2,2,4,3 do not define one-to-one trajectories, and halving inherited zeros does not prohibit newly created zeros or quartets at heights growing with N

downstreamWeightHalving.literalAdmittedWeights: multiplying downstream admitted theta coefficients by 2^(-n) drives them to zero, so the completion does not tend to xi
downstreamWeightHalving.integerPopulation: literal repeated halving is undefined for odd Fibonacci cohorts without a rounding, pairing or fractional-weight rule
downstreamWeightHalving.remainingDeficits: halving g=1-a gives g_n=2^(-n)g and a_n=1-2^(-n)g, which tends to full admission and preserves the xi limit

remainingIntervalHalving.equivalence: when a is the admitted fraction and g=1-a, remaining-interval halving is exactly remaining-deficit halving
remainingIntervalHalving.zeroConsequence: no horizontal zero contraction follows unless TTI derives a map from a to Re(s)-1/2

finiteCompletion.limit: halved downstream deficits tend to zero, so fixed carrier coefficients tend to one and the scalar families tend locally uniformly to xi

logicalAssessment.strongConditionalResult: same-xi horizontal halving would prove RH immediately by finite accumulation
missingConditions: a TTI derivation that the splice at 1 acts on horizontal zero displacement
proof that the halving image of every xi zero is another zero of the same xi function
or a global all-zero shrinking strip for every finite completion, not merely tracked zeros
a rule preventing newly created zeros and escaping quartets
an integer or fractional interpretation if carrier populations themselves halve
logicalAssessment.status: the proposed rule identifies an RH-equivalent contraction, but does not yet derive it
